When a Muslim slapped a Jew in a quarrel over Moses, the Prophet forbade preferring him to Moses, whom he will find holding the Throne on Resurrection.
Angels guard Medina, and if Allah wills neither the Dajjal nor plague will come near it.
Every prophet has one invocation surely answered, and the Prophet wishes, if Allah wills, to keep his as intercession for his followers on Resurrection.
The Prophet dreamt he drew water from a well, then Abu Bakr drew a bucket or two weakly, and Umar, with a huge bucket, watered the people and camels.
When someone in need came, the Prophet told his companions to intercede for him and be rewarded, for Allah fulfils what He wills through His Messenger's tongue.
No one should say to Allah 'forgive me if You wish', but ask firmly, for Allah does what He wills and none can force Him.
Told that Allah's slave Khadir was more learned, Moses sought him with a fish as the sign, finding him by retracing their steps to where it was lost.
The Prophet said they would camp at Khaif Bani Kinana tomorrow if Allah willed, and at the siege of Ta'if said they would return home tomorrow if Allah willed.
When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, angels beat their wings at His word; when their fear passes they ask what their Lord said and are told the truth.
Allah listens to nothing as He listens to the Prophet reciting the Quran aloud in a pleasant voice.
On Resurrection Allah will call Adam, and a voice will order him to bring out from his offspring those sent to the Fire.
Aisha was never as jealous of any woman as of Khadija, whom Allah ordered the Prophet to give glad tidings of a palace in Paradise.
When Allah loves someone He tells Gabriel, who loves him and announces it in the heavens, then earth's people welcome him; angels of night and day report His slaves praying.
Gabriel brought the Prophet glad tidings that whoever dies worshipping nothing besides Allah will enter Paradise, even if he stole or committed illegal intercourse.
The Prophet taught a bedtime invocation of surrender and trust in Allah, and on the Day of the Clans asked Allah, Revealer of the Book, to defeat and shake them.
The verse forbidding prayer too loud or too low came while the Prophet hid in Mecca: recite so companions hear, but not pagans, who abused the Quran.
Allah said the son of Adam hurts Him by abusing Time, for He is Time: all things are in His Hands and He alternates night and day.
Allah said the fast is for Him, the faster leaving desire, food and drink for Him; it shields from Hell, and the faster's breath is better to Allah than musk.
Job gathered gold locusts falling on him as he bathed; asked by his Lord whether He had not made him rich enough, he said he could not forgo His blessings.
Every night in its last third the Lord descends to the nearest heaven and asks who will invoke, ask or seek forgiveness, that He may answer, grant and forgive.
The Prophet said Muslims are the last but will be foremost on Resurrection; the narrators add that Allah tells man to spend, promising to compensate him.
Gabriel told the Prophet to convey her Lord's greeting to Khadija as she brought food, with glad tidings of a palace of Qasab in Paradise without noise or fatigue.
Allah said He has prepared for His righteous slaves what no eye has seen, no ear heard and no heart imagined.
In night prayer the Prophet praised Allah as Light and Lord of the heavens and earth, affirmed His promise, Paradise, Hell and the Hour are true, and sought forgiveness.
Slandered, Aisha hoped Allah would clear her through a dream of the Prophet, never thinking He would reveal verses to be recited, but He revealed ten verses of Surat an-Nur.
A bad deed only intended is not written, and abandoned for Allah's sake it counts as good; a good deed intended counts as one, and done, ten to seven hundred.
When creation was finished, the womb sought Allah's refuge from those who sever it, and He promised to join whoever joins it and cut whoever cuts it.
When it rained after the Prophet's invocation, he said Allah declared that some of His slaves had become disbelievers in Him and some believers.
Allah loves meeting whoever loves meeting Him, dislikes meeting whoever dislikes it, and is to His slave as the slave thinks of Him.
Allah forgave a man who had his body burned and the ashes scattered out of fear of Him, and forgives a slave who sins and asks forgiveness again and again.
The Prophet will intercede repeatedly until those with faith of a mustard seed leave Hell; on a fourth plea Allah will take out all who said La ilaha illallah.
The last man to leave Hell is given Paradise ten times the world; each person's Lord will speak to him, Fire ahead, so shield yourself even with half a date.
A Jewish priest said on Resurrection Allah will hold all creation on His fingers saying 'I am the King'; the Prophet smiled, amazed and believing, and recited a verse.
Each person will come close to his Lord, who will screen him from others, make him confess his sins, and forgive them as He screened them in the world.
Moses blamed Adam for turning his offspring out of Paradise; Adam answered that Moses blamed him for what was ordained before his creation, and so Adam prevailed.
Believers gathered on Resurrection will ask Adam, father of mankind, to intercede with their Lord, and he will say he is not fit, mentioning his mistake.
Gabriel opened the Prophet's chest at Zamzam and took him up the seven heavens meeting prophets; the fifty prayers were reduced to five, rewarded as fifty, before he woke.
Allah will grant the people of Paradise His lasting pleasure, and a man there who wishes to farm will see his crop grow and be harvested in moments, mountain-high.
The greatest sin is setting up rivals to Allah who created you, then killing your son for fear he will share your food, then illegal intercourse with your neighbour's wife.
Three men at the Ka'ba argued whether Allah hears them when they speak softly, and Allah revealed the verse that their ears, eyes and skins would testify against them.
